rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called al-Inshirah in most tafsirs and the two cited hadith collections, al-Sharh in some sources, and al-Inshirah in others.
rows.anchor: سميت في معظم التفاسير وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) و ( جامع الترمذي ) ( سورة ألم نشرح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is Meccan by consensus, the twelfth revealed after al-Duha and before al-Asr, and has eight verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . وقد عدت الثانية عشرة

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz treated al-Inshirah as part of al-Duha and recited both in one obligatory prayer unit without a division.
rows.anchor: وعن طاوس وعمر بن عبد العزيز أنهما كانا يقولان : ( ألم نشرح من سورة الضحى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls that practice anomalous and contrary to the community's agreement on the codex's surah divisions.
rows.anchor: وهذا شذوذ مخالف لما اتفقت عليه الأمة من تسوير المصحف الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah recalls God's gentle care, relief of the Prophet's grief and hardship, clarification, and elevation of his standing.
rows.anchor: احتوت على ذكر عناية الله تعالى لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلطف الله له وإزالة الغم والحرج عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its message serves as evidence for al-Duha: past care reassures the Prophet that the One who began blessing him will continue it.
rows.anchor: فمضمونها شبيه بأنه حجة على مضمون سورة الضحى تثبيتا له بتذكيره سالف عنايته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It promises ease whenever hardship comes, urging the Prophet to endure the mission's burdens and seek God's help.
rows.anchor: واتبع ذلك بوعده بأنه كلما عرض له عسر فسيجد من أمره يسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a confirmatory question phrased negatively, intended to affirm what was denied and remind the Prophet of this favor.
rows.anchor: استفهام تقريري على النفي . والمقصود التقرير على إثبات المنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder should keep him active in his great call rather than grieving over the people he seeks to guide.
rows.anchor: ليدوم على دعوته العظيمة نشيطا غير ذي أسف ولا كمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharh literally means separating pieces of flesh; applying it to inward satisfaction is either a common near-literal usage or a metaphor.
rows.anchor: فصل أجزاء اللحم بعضها عن بعض ، ومنه الشريحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor likely extends bodily constriction to grief, making removal of sorrow like opening flesh; this best suits the following promise of ease.
rows.anchor: فجعل إزالة ما في النفس من حزن مثل شرح اللحم وهذا الأنسب بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the imagery of a constricted chest with the verse about the Prophet's chest being tight at what people say, and recalls Moses' prayer in Ta-Ha.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز } ( هود : 12 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest denotes the inward faculty encompassing reason and perception; its opening signifies gifts of spiritual perfection, God's approval, and future success for the religion.
rows.anchor: فالصدر مراد به الإحساس الباطني الجامع لمعنى العقل والإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is his reading from the verse's wording and structure, independent of external reports.
rows.anchor: هذا تفسير الآية بما يفيده نظمها واستقلالها عن المرويات الخارجية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the opening of the chest as God opening the Prophet's heart to Islam.
rows.anchor: ففسرها ابن عباس بأن الله شرح قلبه بالإسلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's chest was filled with knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن قال : شرح صدره أن ملىء علما وحكما

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustari interprets it as the light of the message; many exegetes adopted this reading, which Ibn Atiyya attributed to the majority.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله التستري : شرح صدره بنور الرسالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A bodily interpretation is also possible and is reported from Ibn Abbas: the verse alludes to the Prophet's sacred chest-splitting.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل الشرح شرحا بدنيا . وروي عن ابن عباس أنه فسر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports in the two Sahih collections and longer sira and musnad versions differ on whether the chest-splitting occurred in a dream, while awake, or between sleep and wakefulness.
rows.anchor: فوقع بعض الروايات في ( الصحيحين ) أنه كان في رؤيا النوم ورؤيا الأنبياء وحي

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: In a Muslim report, Anas says he saw the mark of the incision on the Prophet's chest; versions also differ on its time and place while locating it in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث مسلم عن أنس بن مالك أنه قال : رأيت أثر الشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the reports differ, some scholars held that the chest-splitting happened two to four times, including once while the Prophet was with Halima.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الروايات حمل بعض أهل العلم على القول بأن شق صدره الشريف تكرر مرتين إلى أربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse promises that God will make each difficulty facing the Prophet easy; with signals ease follows closely after hardship or its first signs.
rows.anchor: فاليسر لا يتخلف عن اللحاق بتلك المصاعب ، وذلك من خصائص كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hardship and ease are opposites, their literal simultaneity is impossible; maʿa is metaphorical for ease's near arrival after hardship.
rows.anchor: وكلمة { مع } هنا مستعملة في غير حقيقة معناها لأن العسر واليسر نقيضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading reconciles the verse with the general promise that God will bring ease after hardship in al-Talaq; the intervals can vary.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يندفع التعارض بين هذه الآية وبين قوله تعالى : { سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in hardship refers to the Prophet's known hardship, with al functioning like a genitive replacement in a Kufa grammarian analysis; this keeps the surah focused on his honor.
rows.anchor: تعريف العهد ، أي العسر الذي عهدته وعلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to make the Prophet's difficulties easy continues the earlier promise, “We shall ease you toward ease.”
rows.anchor: وعد الله تعالى نبيئه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن الله جعل الأمور العسرة عليه يسرة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna marks the news as important. The fa remains because it supplies the resumptive consequence as well as causation, which inna alone would lose.
rows.anchor: وحرف { إن } للاهتمام بالخبر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “ease” magnifies the relief, which overwhelms hardship; the promise may extend to the community because the Prophet's trials concern the mission and Muslims.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { يسرا } للتعظيم ، أي مع العسر العارض لك تيسيرا عظيما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report through Yunus and Maʿmar from al-Hasan attributes to the Prophet the glad tidings that ease has come and one hardship cannot overcome two eases; Ibn Ashur takes this as including the community.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جرير عن يونس ومعمر عن الحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In the Muwatta, Abu Ubayda wrote Umar about Roman forces and fears; Umar replied that God gives a believing servant relief after hardship and one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الموطإ ) ( أن أبا عبيدة بن الجراح كتب إلى عمر بن الخطاب يذكر له جموعا من الروم

rows.speaker: عائذ بن شريح
rows.claim: Aʿidh ibn Shurayh reports from Anas that the Prophet said if hardship entered a rock, ease would enter after it and drive hardship out; then the two verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says he knows no transmitter of this Anas report except Aʿidh ibn Shurayh.
rows.anchor: قال البزار : لا نعلم رواه عن أنس إلا عائذ بن شريح

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
rows.claim: Abu Hatim al-Razi judged the Aʿidh ibn Shurayh hadith weak, as quoted by Ibn Kathir.
rows.anchor: وقد قال أبو حاتم الرازي : في حديث عائذ بن شريح ضعف

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits a similar report from Ibn Masʿud as a Companion statement, not as a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جرير مثله عن ابن مسعود موقوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ease promise may be a parenthesis between the Prophet's raised reputation and the command to resume striving, teaching that no hardship lacks some accompanying ease; otherwise people would perish.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة : { فإن مع العسر يسرا } معترضة بين جملة { ورفعنا لك ذكرك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's gentleness prevents hardship from being unrelieved, as reflected in the statement that if God punished people for wrongdoing He would leave no creature alive.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى { ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة } ( النحل : 61 )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the divine saying that God created one hardship and two eases, so hardship cannot overcome both.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس : يقول الله تعالى خلقت عسرا واحدا وخلقت يسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardship is difficulty in obtaining a desired goal; ease is the opposite, obtaining it readily without effort.
rows.anchor: والعسر : المشقة في تحصيل المرغوب والعملل المقصود .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes assign worldly ease to the first clause and afterlife ease to the second, but the Arabic structure makes the latter pure emphasis.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل اليسر في الجملة الأولى يسر الدنيا وفي الجملة الثانية يسر الآخرة وأسلوب الكلام العربي لا يساعد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule that a repeated definite noun is identical and an indefinite one different does not establish “two eases”: it concerns an indefinite later made definite by the covenant article, in another sentence.
rows.anchor: وبناء كلامهم على قاعدة إعادة النكرة معرفة خطأ لأن تلك القاعدة في إعادة النكرة معرفة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسين الجرجاني
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Husayn al-Jurjani had already refuted that grammatical argument in al-Nazm; al-Kashshaf also rejects it, and Ibn Hisham calls the rule mistaken.
rows.anchor: وقد أبطله من قبل أبو علي الحسين الجرجاني في كتاب ( النظم ) كما في ( معالم التنزيل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second sentence emphasizes the judgment that ease accompanies hardship; “two eases” is a symbolic dual for ease's preponderance, not a count derived from definiteness.
rows.anchor: فكان التأكيد مفيدا ترجيح أثر اليسر على أثر العسر ، وذلك الترجيح عبر عنه بصيغة التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual can suggest repeated abundance: as “look twice” in al-Mulk means look repeatedly, and expressions such as labbayk use repetition that implies strength.
rows.anchor: فإن التثنية قد يكنى بها عن التكرير المراد منه التكثير كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “one hardship, two eases” interpretation is not derived from the definite article on hardship or the indefinite form of ease.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك مستفادا من تعريف { العسر } باللام ولا من تنكير ( اليسر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next command follows from recalling God's care and promise to ease what is difficult in the Prophet's obedience and tireless delivery of the message.
rows.anchor: تفريع على ما تقرر من التذكير باللطف والعناية ووعده وبتيسير ما هو عسير عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faragh literally means the interior of a vessel or container being empty.
rows.anchor: والفراغ : خلو باطن الظرف أو الإناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called Wa-l-Tin in most tafsir books and codices, al-Tin in some sources including al-Tirmidhi's heading, and it is Meccan according to most scholars.
rows.anchor: سميت في معظم كتب التفسير ومعظم المصاحف ( سورة والتين ) بإثبات الواو تسمية بأول كلمة فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says he knows no disagreement among exegetes over its Meccan status; al-Qurtubi reports a Madinan view from Qatada and Ibn Abbas, but the sound report from Ibn Abbas says Meccan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : لا أعرف في ذلك خلافا بين المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the twenty-eighth surah in revelation order, after al-Buruj and before al-Ilaf, and has eight verses.
rows.anchor: وعدت الثامنة والعشرين في ترتيب نزول السور ، نزلت بعد سورة البروج وقبل سورة الإيلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah presents Islam as humanity's sound primordial nature and treats departures from its foundations as corruption and misguidance.
rows.anchor: احتوت هذه السورة على التنبيه بأن الله خلق الإنسان على الفطرة المستقيمة ليعلموا أن الإسلام هو الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's sacred places gesture toward four stages of divine law, suggesting Islam confirms those traditions and shares their foundations.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بالأمور المقسم بها إلى أطوار الشرائع الأربعة إيماء إلى أن الإسلام جاء مصدقا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns those who reject Islam.
rows.anchor: والتعريض بالوعيد للمكذبين بالإسلام .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also reminds people of the favor of being created with an excellent bodily and psychological order.
rows.anchor: وشملت الامتنان على الإنسان بخلقه على أحسن نظام في جثمانه ونفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An emphatic opening oath marks the subject's importance, while its length builds anticipation for the sworn statement.
rows.anchor: ابتداء الكلام بالقسم المؤكد يؤذن بأهمية الغرض المسوق له الكلام ، وإطالة القسم تشويق إلى المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig's form, dark peel, honeyed interior, pleasant taste, and easy cultivation display God's precise craft, knowledge, and power, and are a blessing to people.
rows.anchor: فحالتها دالة على دقة صنع الله ومؤذنة بعلمه وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah praises the fine reward of people who follow Islam in its foundations and branches.
rows.anchor: والتنويه بحسن جزاء الذين اتبعوا الإسلام في أصوله وفروعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath at places associated with major revealed religions is a fine opening for the surah's claim that humanity was created in sound nature, able to recognize the Creator and His unity.
rows.anchor: وفي ابتداء السورة بالقسم بما يشمل إرادة مهابط أشهر الأديان الإلاهية براعة استهلال لغرض السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath hints that doctrines departing from the foundations of all divine laws have deviated, despite differences in their branches; even this possibility suffices for the opening's rhetorical effect.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى أن ما خالف ذلك من النحل والملل قد حاد عن أصول شرائع الله كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that humanity was created in the best constitution, together with what follows, answers the oath.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } مع ما عطف عليه هو جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The constitution and subsequent return are subtle, inward matters requiring reflection, so the oath's emphatic force is apt when most people act as if they deny their natural disposition.
rows.anchor: والقسم عليه يدل على أن التقويم تقويم خفي وأن الرد رد خفي يجب التدبر لإدراكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates the foundational causes at humanity's beginning and the causes by which descendants develop from them.
rows.anchor: وخلق الله جميع الناس هو أنه خلق أصول الإيجاد وأوجد الأصول الأولى في بدء الخليقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links creation to God's statement that He created Adam with His hands and to the creation and shaping of humanity before commanding the angels to bow.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { لما خلقت بيدي } ( ص : 75 ) وخلق أسباب تولد الفروع من الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan may be a generic noun covering all people, or a name for human nature itself regardless of changes affecting individuals, as in the verse “the human was created anxious.”
rows.anchor: وتعريف { الإنسان } يجوز أن يكون تعريف الجنس ، وهو التعريف الملحوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The essence reading is like “man is better than woman,” or Imru al-Qays's line that war is initially young, and resembles the use in al-Maʿarij.
rows.anchor: ومنه التعريف الواقع في قوله تعالى : { إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwim means placing something in balanced, sound form; the best constitution is the most complete and fitting form for humanity, unlike other creatures.
rows.anchor: والتقويم : جعل الشيء في قوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This human distinction lies in harmonizing outward and inward faculties so none corrupts the person or obstructs another faculty's function.
rows.anchor: في تعديل القوى الظاهرة والباطنة بحيث لا تكون إحدى قواه موقعة له فيما يفسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fi is figurative for secure possession or attachment; choosing it over a more direct preposition conveys stronger connection concisely.
rows.anchor: وحرف { في } يفيد الظرفية المجازية المستعارة لمعنى التمكن والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes a human constitution fitted to the capacities needed for the species' order and civilization, not physical beauty by itself.
rows.anchor: فأفادت الآية أن الله كون الإنسان تكوينا ذاتيا متناسبا ما خلق له نوعه من الإعداد لنظامه وحضارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodily appearance is not God's criterion for improving the soul, helping others, or reforming the earth; the Prophet says God looks at hearts, not bodies or forms.
rows.anchor: وليس تقويم صورة الإنسان الظاهرة هو المعتبر عند الله تعالى ولا جديرا بأن يقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound perception and reason are God's intended excellence because bodily actions proceed from reason and the body serves it; intellect is humanity's noblest gift.
rows.anchor: فالمرضي عند الله هو تقويم إدراك الإنسان ونظره العقلي الصحيح لأن ذلك هو الذي تصدر عنه أعمال الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the best constitution as bodily form and the return as old age does not fit the surah's purpose or warrant its emphatic oath.
rows.anchor: وأما خلق جسد الإنسان في أحسن تقويم فلا ارتباط له بمقصد السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for believers shows that faith is the fruit of rational constitution: it guides conduct and good treatment of people who share the truth.
rows.anchor: ويدل لذلك قوله بعده : { إلا الذين آمنوا } ( التين : 6 ) لأن الإيمان أثر التقويم لعقل الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This nature may be disrupted before birth by parental disease or injury to the fetus, and after birth by serious illness that distorts temperament.
rows.anchor: فذلك هو الأصل في تكوين الإنسان إذا سلم من عوارض عائقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long-term intoxicants or drugs can also damage a person's reasoning or weaken resolve and divert the natural constitution.
rows.anchor: ومما يدخله على نفسه من مساوي العادات كشرب المسكرات وتناول المخدرات مما يورثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To fit the old-age interpretation to the surah's aim, one would have to read the lowering as an ungrateful response to a blessing that brings a person low.
rows.anchor: ولا يلائم مقصد السورة إلا أن يتأول بأن ذلك ذكر نعمة على الإنسان عكس الإنسان شكرها

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: As transmitted by Ibn Atiyya from al-Thaʿlabi, Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says the best human constitution consists in intellect and perception adorned with discrimination.
rows.anchor: ما حكاه ابن عطية عن الثعلبي عن أبي بكر بن طاهر أنه قال

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm interprets the best constitution as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge, and eloquence.
rows.anchor: وما حكاه الفخر عن الأصم أن { أحسن تقويم } أكمل عقل وفهم وأدب وعلم وبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature inclines to benefit and goodness, rejects perceived falsehood or harm, and ordinarily delights in justice, helping the vulnerable, kindness, and honest counsel.
rows.anchor: وتفيد الآية أن الإنسان مفطور على الخير وأن في جبلته جلب النفع والصلاح لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-interest, appetite, or anger can temporarily block this disposition; when bad desire wins, people do evil and resist advice in proportion to its control of reason.
rows.anchor: فإذا ساورته الشهوة السيئة فزينت له ارتكاب المفاسد ولم يستطع ردها عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most jurists and hadith scholars therefore hold that people begin in goodness, uprightness, sound judgment, and good intention.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان الأصل في الناس الخير والعدالة والرشد وحسن النية عند جمهور من الفقهاء والمحدثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about being returned low is coordinated with creation and remains under the oath; its pronoun refers to the human defined in either of the two earlier senses.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } معطوفة على جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks a higher-order delay: reversal from the best created state to the lowest is startling, and changing an existing state is more astonishing than originating one.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } لإفادة التراخي الرتبي كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God made the human low or placed him among the lowest; radd figuratively means turning something into a different state.
rows.anchor: ولقد صيرناه أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfal is a superlative for the most base, and “lowest of the low” means low in belief in the Creator, as the next exception for believers indicates.
rows.anchor: فالمراد : أسفل سافلين في الإعتقاد بخالقه بقرينة قوله : { إلا الذين آمنوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufliyya literally means low location but commonly signifies baseness of character; the phrase is the second object of radd, construed like verbs of becoming.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة السفالة : انخفاض المكان ، وتطلق مجازا شائعا على الخسة والحقارة في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fall from their innate monotheism and reverent awareness by worshipping stones, animals, trees, time, or denying the Maker despite seeing creation and themselves.
rows.anchor: من بقر أو تماسيح أو ثعابين أو من شجر السمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts denial of the Creator with the reminder to look within oneself for signs.
rows.anchor: أو من يجحد وجود الصانع وهو يشاهد مصنوعاته ويحس بوجود نفسه قال تعالى : { وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human ethical degradation includes flattering from greed, stinginess from fear, panic, sacrificing people to idols, burying daughters, and burning widows with dead husbands.
rows.anchor: فمن ملق إذا طمع ، ومن شح إذا شجع ، ومن جزع إذا خاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the return to God is figurative: He establishes high-level causes and their interactions that lead through subsidiary causes to immediate causes.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الرد إلى الله تعالى إسناد مجازي لأنه يكون الأسباب العالية ونظام تفاعلها وتقابلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is like attributing the extension and gradual withdrawal of a shadow to God, or saying a prince built a city.
rows.anchor: على نحو إسناد مد وقبض الظل إليه تعالى في قوله : { ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, asfal safilin is an adverbial place lower than the lowest inhabitants, the abode of punishment; on this reading radd means placing someone where deserved and God's agency is literal.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أسفل سافلين } ظرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place reading is the lowest part of the Fire, as in the verse about hypocrites being in its lowest depth.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو دار العذاب كقوله : { إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار }

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Uways recounts Rabiʿa asking Malik who is base: Malik answered one who earns through religion, and the basest of the base exploits others' religion; Rabiʿa approved.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي أويس : قال مالك : أقبل علي يوما ربيعة فقال لي : من السفلة يا مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this teaching to polytheists whose leaders misled them into idol worship to secure their own leadership.
rows.anchor: وأن المشركين كانوا أسفل سافلين لأنهم ضللهم كبراؤهم وأيمتهم فسولوا لهم عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is connected to the general term “human”: nonbelievers remain low, while people who believe return from shirk to their original fitra.
rows.anchor: استثناء متصل من عموم الإنسان فلما أخبر عن الإنسان بأنه رد أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers regain the original best constitution, and righteous deeds deepen the fitra and guide it toward additional virtues.
rows.anchor: صاروا بالإيمان إلى الفطرة التي فطر الله الإنسان عليها فراجعوا أصلهم إلى أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction of righteous works praises believers because faith motivates action; this describes the believers at the surah's revelation.
rows.anchor: فكان عطف { وعملوا الصالحات } للثناء على المؤمنين بأن إيمانهم باعث لهم على العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception cannot be detached from its general term because the fa in “for them is a reward” rules that reading out.
rows.anchor: وليس لانقطاع الاستثناء هنا احتمال لأن وجود الفاء في قوله : { فلهم أجر غير ممنون } يأباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first three descriptions are joined by fa, the usual Arabic pattern for successive adjectives or places; it usually marks sequential occurrence here and in Ibn Ziyaba's verse, but may mark mention order in al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: وعطفت هذه الأوصاف الثلاثة الأولى بالفاء لأن أسلوب العرب في عطف الصفات وعطف الأمكنة أن يكون بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa introducing the stirred dust attaches the result to the raiding description: dust and reaching the crowd follow the dawn raid, rather than being independent oath objects.
rows.anchor: والفاء العاطفة لقوله : { فأثرن به نقعا } عاطفة على وصف ( المغيرات )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from active participles to two past-tense verbs moves from the oath to a narrative of the results of charging, sparking, and raiding: reaching the target.
rows.anchor: فلذلك غير الأسلوب في قوله : { فأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا } فجيء بهما فعلين ماضيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the chargers are warhorses, the target is an enemy settlement; if they are pilgrims' camels, dust rises on arrival and the “gathering” may be Muzdalifah.
rows.anchor: إذا كان المراد ب { العاديات } الخيل ، أو بلوغ تمام الحج

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali interpreted the chargers as pilgrimage mounts; that reading makes the oath by pilgrimage rites persuasive to disbelievers who deny the Qur'an's divine origin.
rows.anchor: وهو الوجه الذي فسر به علي بن أبي طالب هو أن يصدق المشركون بوقوع المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the chargers are raiding horses, the oath alarms disbelievers with a looming raid, identified as Badr, while reassuring the Prophet about the troop he sent with al-Mundhir ibn Amr, if its report is sound.
rows.anchor: فالقسم بها لأجل التهويل والترويع لإشعار المشركين بأن غارة تترقبهم وهي غزوة بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific horse oath also embeds reassurance for the Prophet about the dispatched unit's fate.
rows.anchor: مع تسكين نفس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من التردد في مصير السرية التي بعث بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain clause is parenthetical between the people scattering and the heavy scales, adding terror; the likeness concerns dense crowding on the gathering plain.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش } معترضة بين جملة { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ahn means wool, perhaps specifically red-dyed or multicolored wool; Zuhayr's poetry supports the colored sense because mountains vary in color.
rows.anchor: والعهن : الصوف ، وقيل : يختص بالمصبوغ الأحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manfush is wool separated into loose fibers for spinning or stuffing; the comparison is to mountains breaking into scattered fragments.
rows.anchor: والمنفوش : المفرق بعض أجزائه عن بعض ليغزل أو تحشى به الحشايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “become” distinguishes creation from dissolution, each marking the end of one world and appearance of another.
rows.anchor: وإعادة كلمة { تكون } مع حرف العطف للإشارة إلى اختلاف الكونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of mountains like wool was also discussed in al-Maʿarij.
rows.anchor: وتقدم قوله تعالى : { وتكون الجبال كالعهن } في سورة المعارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two outcomes detail the general human condition at the gathering, dividing people into a good and a frightening state.
rows.anchor: تفصيل لما في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث } ( القارعة : 4 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales figuratively signal God's approval through abundant good deeds; Arabic uses weight for merit and honor, so the deeds need not be named explicitly.
rows.anchor: وثقل الموازين كناية عن كونه بمحل الرضى من الله تعالى لكثرة حسناته

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says no sound hadith establishes the scale's physical nature; the point is that no deed is lost, which God can realize by an instrument, angels, or another means.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي في ( العواصم ) : لم يرد حديث صحيح في الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most codices and tafsirs, including al-Tirmidhi's heading, call it al-Takathur; some call it Alhakum, as al-Bukhari titles it, while companions reportedly called it al-Maqbara.
rows.anchor: وسميت في معظم المصاحف ومعظم التفاسير ( سورة التكاثر ) وكذلك عنونها الترمذي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
rows.claim: Said ibn Abi Hilal reports that the Prophet's companions called the surah al-Maqbara.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن أبي هلال : كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمونها ( المقبرة )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil report a Meccan occasion involving a rivalry between Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm; al-Qurtubi attributes the account to them and Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل : أنها نزلت في مفاخرة جرت بين بني عبد مناف وبني سهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Itqan prefers a Madinan setting, citing a report about two Ansari clans and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's statement that Muslims had recited a saying about Adam's wealth as Qur'an until this surah came.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) : المختار أنها مدنية . قال : ويدل له ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ubayy report does not prove a Madinan revelation: “we” could mean Muslims generally, who had mistaken a saying for Qur'an until the Prophet clarified it.
rows.anchor: إذ يجوز أن يريد بضمير كنا } المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning's severe tone and content indicate a Meccan audience of polytheists, since the behavior described does not fit Muslims at that time.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر من معاني السورة وغلظة وعيدها أنها مكية وأن المخاطب بها فريق من المشركين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The reported rivalry had Banu Abd Manaf count living nobles, then their dead; Banu Sahm surpassed them by three graves because their pre-Islamic numbers had been greater.
rows.anchor: ثم قالوا نعد موتانا حتى زاروا القبور فعدوا القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi and al-Baghawi transmit the rivalry account from Muqatil and al-Kalbi, with al-Qurtubi also citing them and Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها فيما قاله الواحدي والبغوي عن مقاتل والكلبي والقرطبي عنهما وعن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو بريدة الجرمي
rows.claim: Abu Burayda al-Jurmi reports that Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith of the Ansar boasted of living people, then pointed to notable graves in each group; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بريدة الجرمي قال : نزلت في قبيلين من الأنصار بني حارثة وبني الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Meccan chronology, it is the sixteenth surah revealed, after al-Kawthar and before al-Maʿun, and has eight verses.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت السادسة عشرة في ترتيب نزول السور ، نزلت بعد سورة الكوثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah rebukes neglect of Qur'anic evidence and Islam's call in favor of wealth, accumulation, and ancestral boasting until death, and warns against that course.
rows.anchor: اشتملت على التوبيخ على اللهو عن النظر في دلائل القرآن ودعوة الإسلام بإيثار المال والتكاثر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It urges reflection on what can save people from Hell.
rows.anchor: وحثهم على التدبر فيما ينجيهم من الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It teaches that people will be resurrected and questioned for neglecting gratitude to the great Benefactor.
rows.anchor: وأنهم مبعوثون ومسؤولون عن إهمال شكر المنعم العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alhakum means that something occupied people and diverted them from what they ought to attend to; takathur is competitive accumulation of desired things.
rows.anchor: { ألهاكم } أي شغلكم عما يجب عليكم الاشتغال به لأن اللهو شغل يصرف عن تحصيل أمر مهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The competition can concern wealth or numbers of children and allies used for prestige, as in the boast about having more wealth and children.
rows.anchor: فمنه تكاثر في الأموال ، ومنه تكاثر في العدد من الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects the numbers boast with the statement that people claimed greater wealth and children and therefore no punishment.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين } ( سبأ : 35 )

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line says he is not the one with the most counted heads, but honor belongs to the larger group, illustrating rivalry in numbers.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعشى : ولست بالأكثر منهم حصى وإنما العزة للكاثر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
rows.claim: Muslim reports that Ibn al-Shikhkhir heard the Prophet recite the verse and explain that a person keeps saying “my wealth,” though only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away remains.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن عبد الله بن الشخير قال : ( انتهيت إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith illustrates one sense of accumulation, selected to suit the occasion of that admonition, and is compatible with the verse.
rows.anchor: فهذا جار مجرى التفسير لمعنى من معاني التكاثر اقتضاه حال الموعظة ساعتئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe threats identify the addressees as polytheists, since this behavior was not a Muslim custom then; wealthy chiefs are especially targeted for preferring comfort to the Prophet's call and suppressing it.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للمشركين بقرينة غلظة الوعيد بقوله : { كلا سوف تعلمون ثم كلا سوف تعلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although directly addressed to polytheists, the warning teaches Muslims to resist love of wealth when it distracts from good and to fear death arriving during heedlessness.
rows.anchor: فيعلمون أنهم محذرون من التلبس بشيء من ذلك فيحذرون من أن يلهيهم حب المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatta may mark the duration of distraction through a person's whole life, not the end of distraction followed by another activity, since all works cease at death.
rows.anchor: أي دام إلهاء التكاثر إلى أن زرتم المقابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, visiting graves means residing in them; “visit” hints that residence is temporary and people will leave them.
rows.anchor: ولكون زيارة المقابر على هذا الوجه عبارة عن الحلول فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense “you visited” treats the future as already past because its occurrence is certain, as in “God's command came.”
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالفعل الماضي في { زرتم } لتنزيل المستقبل منزلة الماضي لأنه محقق وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the endpoint is the object of rivalry: they compete over everything, even graves, as in the report about Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm counting tombs.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الغاية للمتكاثر به الدال عليه التكاثر ، أي بكل شيء حتى بالقبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites al-Nabigha and a line attributed to Isam ibn Ubayd al-Zamani or Hammam al-Raqashi, where a grave stands for its occupant.
rows.anchor: والعرب يكنون بالقبر عن صاحبه قال النابغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maqabir is the plural of maqbara, pronounced with either fat-ha or damma on the b, and means land containing many graves.
rows.anchor: و { المقابر } : جمع مقبرة بفتح الموحدة وبضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is followed by afterlife warning: kalla deters and refutes their obsessive accumulation, sawfa guarantees the promised knowledge, and the omitted object is its evil outcome.
rows.anchor: فأفاد { كلا } زجرا وإبطالا لإنهاء التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “you will know” is evidently the disastrous result of neglecting Islam's call because of rivalry.
rows.anchor: وحدف مفعول { تعلمون } لظهور أن المراد : تعلمون سوء مغبة لهوكم بالتكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “they” before the predicate strengthens the judgment that they perform prayer for show.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي في قوله : { هم يراءون } لتقوية الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the surah or its final three verses are Medinan, “those who pray” means hypocrites who only appear to pray; the verb names the appearance of the act, as “the hypocrites fear” means they seem to fear.
rows.anchor: فأما على القول بأن السورة مدنية أو بأن هذه الآيات الثلاث مدنية يكون المراد بالمصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿun here means charity or zakat; the parallel description of hypocrites says they hold back their hands.
rows.anchor: { ويمنعون الماعون } أي الصدقة أو الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fa makes the show-praying hypocrites part of the deniers of Judgment who mistreat orphans and fail to urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: فلما عرفوا بهذه الخلال كان مفاد فاء التفريع أن أولئك المتظاهرين بالصلاة

rows.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
rows.claim: Hibat Allah ibn Salama says the final three verses were revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul, with a plural expression for one person as in the people of Noah denying the messengers, meaning their messenger.
rows.anchor: وحكى هبة الله بن سلامة في كتاب ( الناسخ والمنسوخ ) : أن هذه الآيات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahw literally means inadvertent forgetfulness, but here it sarcastically means deliberate neglect; genuine forgetfulness in prayer is not the target because it is excused for this community.
rows.anchor: والسهو حقيقته : الذهول عن أمر سبق علمه ، وهو هنا مستعار للإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deliberate-neglect sense parallels “forgetting” one's associates as turning away, and being heedless of signs in al-Aʿraf and Yunus.
rows.anchor: ومثله استعارة الغفلة للإعراض في قوله تعالى : { بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a later revelation is attached to an earlier one, God shapes its wording to fit the connection; the consequential fa is a clue worth watching in such cases.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه إذا أراد الله إنزال شيء من القرآن ملحقا بشيء قبله جعل نظم الملحق مناسبا لما هو متصل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan according to most commentators; Abu Amr al-Dani cites a Madinan view from some scholars, but the Meccan view is more famous and sounder.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية عند جمهور المفسرين وحكى أبو عمرو الداني في كتابه المؤلف في تنزيل القرآن عن بعض العلماء

rows.speaker: جمهور من المتأولين
rows.claim: Most interpreters take al-fajr to mean the familiar dawn that rises each day.
rows.anchor: قال جمهور من المتأولين : { الفجر } هنا المشهور الطالع كل يوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-fajr as the whole daytime.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { الفجر } النهار كله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam identify the sworn dawn as the dawn prayer, whose recitation is the Qur'an of dawn.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضاً وزيد بن أسلم : { الفجر } الذي أقسم الله به ، صلاة الصبح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the oath refers to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إنما أراد فجر يوم النحر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means the dawn of Dhu al-Hijjah.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : المراد فجر ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies it as the dawn of the night at Jamʿ, meaning Muzdalifah.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل المراد فجر ليلة جمع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says it is the dawn of the first day of Muharram, the beginning of the year.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أيضاً : المراد فجر أول يوم من المحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations are the emergence of springs from rocks and, according to Ikrima, the dawn of Friday.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد فجر العيون من الصخور وغيرها ، وقال عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-asr means time or the age, and the word has variant vowel forms; Imru al-Qays's verse refers to a bygone age.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { العصر } : الدهر ، يقال فيه : عصر وعصر بضم العين والصاد ، وقال امرؤ القيس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets al-asr as evening.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : { العصر } العشي

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports asking the Prophet, who said God swears by the end of the day.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب : سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العصر فقال : «أقسم ربكم بآخر النهار

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars, as cited by Abu Ali, say al-asr means daytime and al-ʿashr means nighttime; Humaid ibn Thawr's line calls the two day and night.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء ، وذكره أبو علي : { العصر } : اليوم ، { والعصر } الليلة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Another interpretation assigns al-asr to morning and evening, the two cooler periods.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : { العصر } : بكرة ، والعصر : عشية ، وهما الأبردان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says al-asr is the middle prayer, by which God swears; reports identify it as the afternoon prayer and stress the loss of family and property for missing it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : { العصر } هي الصلاة الوسطى ، أقسم الله تعالى بها
